questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Your rear brake locks by accident on a surface with good traction. What should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake immediately.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop. On a good surface, you can still control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel as long as you stay upright and go straight.

questions.question: Where should a motorcycle rider position themselves in a lane to be most easily seen by other drivers?

options.text: The right side
The center
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following another vehicle because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you pass another vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must stay within the speed limit.
Must drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within posted speed limits. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your body weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Make the motorcycle lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the motorcycle lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn or sudden move, you must get your motorcycle to lean fast in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more it needs to lean.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you are about to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are about to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is harder to see than a car's brake light. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so other drivers notice you are slowing down. This is especially important when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is pulling a trailer, how should the following distance change?

options.text: It should increase.
It should decrease.
It should stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should increase.
questions.explanation: When pulling a trailer, a motorcycle should increase its following distance. The extra weight of the trailer means the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: The lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go ahead with caution.
Turn around and use a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what will you likely need to do?

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Raise the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and the most space around you. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: All curves are different. Choose a lane position that is safe for the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcyclist to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see the motorcyclist.
The motorcyclist cannot read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could hit your motorcycle or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When is a staggered formation not recommended for a group of motorcycles?

options.text: It is recommended at all times.
When entering or leaving a highway.
When riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is generally safe, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Before you start your motorcycle, make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check that your fuel valve is open. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel in the lines, but will stall when that fuel runs out.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Traffic signal ahead.
Stop completely and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol content (BAC) limit for a driver of legal drinking age?

options.text: .02 percent
.08 percent
.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: .08 percent
questions.explanation: A driver of legal drinking age is considered legally intoxicated at .08 percent BAC. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can ignore no-passing zone markings if you started passing in a legal zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead of you.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes at night, slow down and stay farther away from the vehicle ahead. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see the road better. Adjust your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow extra stopping distance. The passenger should grip the passenger handgrips firmly or hold onto your waist, hips, or midsection—not the back of the bike.
